terms.meaning: A saved copy of finished work, so the run can continue from that point.
A number that marks which shape of record a file was written in.
Renaming a file as one step, so a half-written file is never seen under its final name.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and recovery rule
sections.what: Explains that a process is the unit of recovery and that finished records are stored and read back as they were, not recalculated.
sections.why: Recalculating after a restart could give the portfolio two different versions of analysis, which would make the final comparisons unreliable.
sections.watch_out: Anyone changing this file must keep the rule that stored results are read back, not run again.

sections.name: StaleCheckpoint
sections.title: Stale checkpoint error
sections.what: Defines the error raised when a stored record was written under a different schema version.
sections.why: A checkpoint that almost fits would produce a complete-looking portfolio with one record in the wrong shape, which is harder to spot than a visible failure.
sections.watch_out: Catching this error and carrying on would silently mix schema versions.

sections.name: CheckpointStore
sections.title: Checkpoint store contract
sections.what: Lists the three things any store must do: get a record, save a record, and list finished ids for a run.
sections.why: Keeping the contract separate lets the file store and the memory store be swapped without changing the pipeline.
sections.watch_out: The run id is part of every key, so two runs of the same portfolio never share checkpoints.

sections.name: InMemoryCheckpointStore
sections.title: In-memory checkpoint store
sections.what: Keeps finished records in a dictionary for the life of one program run.
sections.why: The docstring says it is for tests and single runs where the failure is a bad response, not a crash. Reason beyond that is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Nothing is saved to disk, so a crash loses all records held here.

sections.name: FileCheckpointStore
sections.title: File checkpoint store
sections.what: Saves one JSON file for each finished process inside a folder named for the run, and reads files back with a schema check.
sections.why: Writing to a temporary file and then renaming it means a crash mid-write leaves no truncated file under the real name. Keys are kept in the original order so the saved bytes match a fresh run.
sections.watch_out: Sorting the keys on write would change the saved bytes and break the byte-identical replay promise.

summary: Saves each finished process analysis to disk so that a failed run can resume without redoing the work already completed.
purpose: Make a run recoverable at the boundary of each process, so one failure does not cost all earlier analyses.
why: Recalculating finished processes under a different model version would mix two versions of analysis in one portfolio. Stored records are read back exactly as they were written.
how: After each process completes, its record is written to a temporary file and then renamed into place. On resume, a stored record is loaded if it exists. If the stored record was written under a different schema version, loading fails with a clear error.
inputs: A run id, a process canonical id, and a completed ProcessRecord.
outputs: A stored ProcessRecord when asked for one, or nothing if the process has not finished. A set of finished process ids for a run.
risks: A checkpoint from an older schema version stops the resume rather than being converted. The in-memory store is lost when the program stops.
debug: If a resume raises StaleCheckpoint, compare the schema version in the stored file with the current build. Look for leftover partial files, which are named with a leading dot and an extension of partial.
